text: The report proposes testing whether the Desulfovibrio vulgaris Hildenborough field-versus-lab pattern generalizes by applying the classification to other environmentally relevant ENIGMA organisms with Fitness Browser data, such as Pseudomonas FW300 strains.
quote: **Multi-organism extension**: Apply the field vs lab classification to other ENIGMA organisms (e.g., *Pseudomonas* FW300 strains) that have both environmental relevance and Fitness Browser data, to test whether the pattern generalizes
heading: Future Directions

text: The report proposes replacing binary core/auxiliary status with the fraction of genomes carrying a gene cluster to increase statistical power in the Desulfovibrio vulgaris Hildenborough conservation analysis.
quote: **Finer-grained conservation metric**: Replace binary core/auxiliary with quantitative conservation (fraction of genomes carrying the gene cluster) to increase statistical power
heading: Future Directions

text: The report proposes using the 213K ASVs and 4,346 field samples in ENIGMA CORAL to test whether Desulfovibrio abundance at Oak Ridge sites correlates with geochemistry conditions tested in the Fitness Browser.
quote: **ENIGMA community data integration**: Use the 213K ASVs and 4,346 field samples in ENIGMA CORAL to ask whether *Desulfovibrio* abundance at Oak Ridge sites correlates with the geochemistry conditions tested in the Fitness Browser
heading: Future Directions

text: The report proposes investigating whether antibiotic and heavy-metal resistance genes in the Desulfovibrio vulgaris Hildenborough accessory genome are on mobile elements, recently acquired, or shared with co-occurring Oak Ridge species.
quote: **Accessory resistance gene characterization**: Deeper analysis of the antibiotic and heavy-metal resistance genes in the accessory genome -- are they on mobile elements? Recently acquired? Shared with co-occurring species at Oak Ridge?
heading: Future Directions

text: The report proposes using continuous fitness scores, such as mean or minimum fitness per condition class, instead of binary important/not-important status as logistic-regression predictors in the Desulfovibrio vulgaris Hildenborough analysis.
quote: **Quantitative fitness scores**: Replace binary important/not-important with continuous fitness scores (e.g., mean or minimum fitness per condition class) as predictors in logistic regression
